CHIEF COMPLAINT
Numbness and tingling in bilateral hands.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Patient is a 60-year-old right-handed male referred for evaluation of numbness and tingling. Symptoms began several weeks ago following a motor vehicle accident in December of the previous year when patient sustained bilateral wrist fractures and head contusion. Symptoms have worsened over the past month. On the right side, numbness and tingling extends from the middle and ring fingers up the forearm. On the left side, symptoms extend from the pinky and ring fingers up the forearm. Patient describes pain as mainly soreness with occasional throbbing and associated weakness, particularly when using the hands. Tingling is more prominent when hands hurt and becomes dull when pain subsides. Symptoms are worse at night and intermittently throughout the day. Patient denies loss of sensation but reports decreased sensitivity. Patient was prescribed nerve pain medication but reports inconsistent use. Currently wears splint on right wrist constantly and left wrist intermittently, which provides some relief. Also reports mild neck stiffness related to head trauma during the accident.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Constitutional: Fatigue and weight gain. GI: Excessive appetite and bloating. Eyes: Floaters. Cardiovascular: Shortness of breath and leg swelling. Endocrine: Always hungry. Skin: Nail bed changes, dryness, and itching. Musculoskeletal: Gout and muscle pain. Remainder of review of systems is negative.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Motor vehicle accident with bilateral wrist fractures and head contusion (December, previous year). Prediabetes (controlled with diet modification). No thyroid issues.

MEDICATIONS
Coreg for hypertension. Lexapro for anxiety. Nerve pain medication (inconsistent use).

ALLERGIES
Not documented.

FAMILY HISTORY
Not documented.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Right-handed. Recent motor vehicle accident in December.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Neurologic examination: Right hand sensation normal except diminished pin prick sensation in third and fourth fingers. Left hand sensation decreased in fourth and fifth fingers. Reflexes 1+ and symmetric in arms, 2+ at knees, toes downgoing bilaterally. Tinel sign positive at bilateral wrists and bilateral elbows. Remainder of examination normal.

RESULTS
Pending EMG testing.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
Bilateral carpal tunnel syndrome, likely secondary to past wrist trauma. Rule out bilateral cubital tunnel syndrome. Plan to schedule EMG test to pinpoint exact location of nerve irritation. Patient to follow up after test results are available. If symptoms persist, consider referral to hand clinic for injections or carpal tunnel release surgery, or referral to orthopedist for same treatment options. Continue wearing bilateral wrist splints. Follow-up appointment after diagnostic studies are completed.
